insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Plan-dependent. Annexure C shows Base Sum Insured options (e.g., Optima Secure: 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs). Final Sum Insured as per Policy Schedule.

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be At Actuals unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: Room rent is payable at actuals unless the Policy Schedule sets a limit. This reduces the chance of out-of-pocket costs due to room category restrictions.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: ICU limit (including ICCU) for bed charges shall be At Actuals unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: ICU/ICCU bed charges are payable at actuals unless the Policy Schedule sets a limit. This helps protect you from high ICU room costs during critical care.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.explanation: Restored sum insured can be used even for the same illness within the same policy year. This is stronger than many plans where restore works only for unrelated illnesses.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Secure Benefit adds extra coverage only after the Base Sum Insured is fully exhausted. This provides an insurer-funded buffer for large or multiple claims in a year.

great.name: Renewal Bonus
great.quote: On Renewal... a sum equal to 50% of the Base Sum Insured... will be added... This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.explanation: On renewal, 50% of the Base Sum Insured is added even if claims were made in the expiring policy. This means your coverage can grow without being reduced due to claims.

great.name: Air Ambulance
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred... towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care...
great.explanation: Emergency air ambulance (airplane/helicopter) expenses are covered. This can be valuable for urgent transfers, though the payable amount may depend on plan limits.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: Expenses related to the surgical treatment of obesity that does not fulfil all the below conditions:
great.explanation: Bariatric/obesity surgery is not covered if the stated conditions are not fulfilled (implying it is covered when conditions are met). This can help if you qualify under the policy’s criteria for obesity surgery.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (unless the Policy Schedule says otherwise). This is a common waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: Listed diseases/procedures are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is broadly in line with market-standard specific illness waiting periods.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, except accidents. This is the standard initial waiting period in most health plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 60 days before admission (unless the Policy Schedule says otherwise). This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 180 days after discharge (unless the Policy Schedule says otherwise). This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred during the Policy Year on Domiciliary Hospitalization...
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization expenses are covered when treatment is taken at home as per policy conditions. This is useful when hospital admission is not possible or not available.

good.name: AYUSH Treatment
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred... for Inpatient Care under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy... up to the Sub-limit specified...
good.explanation: Inpatient AYUSH treatment is covered up to the sub-limit specified. This gives some coverage for alternative systems, but payouts may be capped.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Intravenous fluids, blood transfusion, surgical appliances, allowable consumables and/or enteral feedings.
bad.explanation: Only “allowable consumables” are mentioned as part of covered hospitalization expenses, without confirming that all consumables are covered. In many claims, non-payable consumables can still create out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Def. 8. Co-Payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy...
bad.explanation: Only a definition of co-payment is provided here and no co-pay is stated in this clause. Unless another section applies a co-pay, you should not be charged any percentage share on admissible claims.

unclear.name: NCB
unclear.quote: Cumulative Bonus shall be available only if the Cover is specified to be applicable in the Policy Schedule.
unclear.reference: Section B.1 Base Coverage intro, Page 11
unclear.explanation: Cumulative Bonus is available only if it is shown as applicable in the Policy Schedule. You need to check your schedule to know whether you will get any no-claim increase in sum insured.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
